_comment: Known circular imports, READ AND CLASSIFIED — never exempt. Only shrinks: a cycle that leaves
the tree must leave this file in the same commit, and check-import-cycles.mjs fails if it does
not. A cycle NOT listed here fails immediately.
Measured 2026-08-19 on the first run of the ported check: 17 distinct cycles, four families.
None is a live incident — every one of them compiles and ships today, which is precisely why
they survived. A cycle costs nothing until the first time one side needs a VALUE from the
other; then it becomes a module-initialisation error nowhere near its cause.
FAMILY A — parent declares the shared type, child imports it back (11 of 17).
The shape life-therapy's own first run found. A page or widget declares an interface, and the
components it renders import that type from their parent. Type-only, so TypeScript erases it
and nothing fails. FIX: move the shared type into its own module beside them (LT used
`booking-data.ts`); mechanical, and each one is independent of the others.
Entries 1-8, 10, 11 below.
FAMILY B — the rules plugin registry (4 of 17).
`engine` imports the VALUE `RULE_REGISTRY` from `registry`, `registry` imports each rule
module, and each rule imports its types back from `engine`. This is the standard
plugin-registry loop and the rule->engine edge is type-only. FIX: extract the rule-facing
types into `lib/rules/types.ts` so rules depend on the contract rather than on the engine.
Entries 12-15.
FAMILY C — trust close/export (2 of 17).
`audit-export` imports `type OutstandingItem` from `close`, which calls back into the export.
Type-only, same fix as family A.  Entries 16, 17.
FAMILY D — auth/tier, and the ONE that is not type-only (1 of 17).
`lib/tier/getOrgTier` imports the VALUE `getServerOrgMembership` from `lib/auth/server`,
which reaches back through `can` -> `orgRoles` -> `getOrgTier`. A real runtime loop on the
authorisation path: it works today only because of the order Node happens to initialise these
modules in. Highest priority of the four, and the reason this check is worth its sixty lines.
Entry 9.
